G4672.strongs: Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David
senses: Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in [[r:ACT.3.11|Act 3:11 5:12]]; in [[r:ACT.7.47|Act 7:47]] T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: [[r:MAT.1.6|Mat 1:6-7 6:29 12:42]], [[r:LUK.11.31|Luk 11:31 12:27]], [[r:JHN.10.23|Jhn 10:23]], [[r:ACT.3.11|Act 3:11 5:12 7:47]].† (AS)
(in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: [[r:MAT.2.11|Mat 2:11]], [[r:JHN.19.39|Jhn 19:39]].† (AS)
Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.with, Hdt., al.).† (AS)

G4639.strongs: "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration))
senses: shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: [[r:MRK.4.32|Mrk 4:32]], [[r:ACT.5.15|Act 5:15]]; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, [[r:MAT.4.16|Mat 4:16]], [[r:LUK.1.79|Luk 1:79]]" (LXX).
a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., [[r:HEB.8.5|Heb 8:5]]; opposite to σῶμα, [[r:COL.2.17|Col 2:17]]; opposite to εἰκών, [[r:HEB.10.1|Heb 10:1.]]† (AS)

G4613.strongs: Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites
senses: a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (which see), Simon
One of the Brethren of our Lord (see: ἀδελψός): [[r:MAT.13.55|Mat 13:55]], [[r:MRK.6.3|Mrk 6:3]].
The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (which see): [[r:JHN.6.71|Jhn 6:71 12:4]] (Rec.) 13:2,26

G4624.strongs: to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure)
senses: (σκάνδαλον), prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaphorically of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: with accusative of person(s), [[r:MAT.5.29|Mat 5:29-30 17:27 18:6, 8-9]] [[r:MRK.9.42|Mrk 9:42-43, 45 9:47]] [[r:LUK.17.2|Luk 17:2]], [[r:JHN.6.61|Jhn 6:61]], [[r:1CO.8.13|1Co 8:13]]. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: [[r:MAT.11.6|Mat 11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33]], [[r:MRK.4.17|Mrk 4:17 6:3 14:27, 29]], [[r:LUK.7.23|Luk 7:23]], [[r:JHN.16.1|Jhn 16:1]], [[r:ROM.14.21|Rom 14:21]] (WH, R, txt., om.), [[r:2CO.11.29|2Co 11:29]],† (AS)

G4600.strongs: the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face

G4659.root: from σκυθρός (sullen) and a derivative of [[w:G3700]]
G4659.strongs: angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance

G4655.forms: σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό)

G4687.root: probably strengthened from [[w:G4685]] (through the idea of extending)
G4687.strongs: to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively)

senses: possess. prop. of second of person(s), thy, thine: [[r:MAT.7.3|Mat 7:3]], al.; as subst., οἱ σοί, thy kinsfolk, friends, [[r:MRK.5.19|Mrk 5:19]]; τὸ σόν, what is thine, [[r:MAT.20.14|Mat 20:14 25:25]]; τὰ σά, thy goods, [[r:LUK.6.30|Luk 6:30]] (AS)

G4697.strongs: to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity
senses: σπλαγχνίζομαι (σπλάγχνον), to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., [[r:LUK.10.33|Luk 10:33 15:20]]; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., [[r:MAT.18.27|Mat 18:27 20:34]], [[r:MRK.1.41|Mrk 1:41]]; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), [[r:MAT.14.14|Mat 14:14]], [[r:LUK.7.13|Luk 7:13]]; ἐπί, with accusative, [[r:MAT.15.32|Mat 15:32]], [[r:MRK.6.34|Mrk 6:34 8:2 9:22]]; ωερί, [[r:MAT.9.36|Mat 9:36.]] (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: [[r:1KI.23.21|1Ki 23:21]], [[r:EZK.24.21|Eze 24:21]], Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on [[r:PHP.1.8|Php 1:8]], in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) † (AS)
in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.).

In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), [[r:MRK.5.35|Mrk 5:35]], [[r:LUK.8.49|Luk 8:49]]; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, [[r:MAT.9.36|Mat 9:36]]; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, [[r:LUK.7.6|Luk 7:6]] (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).† (AS)

G4670.strongs: Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine

G4678.strongs: wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual)
senses: skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense;

of human wisdom: [[r:1CO.2.1|1Co 2:1 2:4-5]], [[r:JAS.3.15|Jas 3:15]], [[r:REV.13.18|Rev 13:18 17:9]]; σ. Σολομῶνος, [[r:MAT.12.42|Mat 12:42]], [[r:LUK.11.31|Luk 11:31]]; Αἰγυπτίων, [[r:ACT.7.22|Act 7:22]]; Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, [[r:1CO.1.22|1Co 1:22]]; σ. λόγου, [[r:1CO.1.17|1Co 1:17]]; τ. σοφῶν, [[r:1CO.1.19|1Co 1:19]] (LXX); τ. κόσμου, [[r:1CO.1.20|1Co 1:20-21 3:19]]; ἀνθρωπίνη, [[r:1CO.2.13|1Co 2:13]]; σαρκική, [[r:2CO.1.12|2Co 1:12]]; of wisdom in spiritual things: [[r:LUK.21.15|Luk 21:15]], [[r:ACT.6.3|Act 6:3, 10 7:10]], [[r:1CO.2.6|1Co 2:6]], [[r:COL.1.28|Col 1:28 2:23 3:16 4:5]], [[r:JAS.1.5|Jas 1:5 3:13, 17]], [[r:2PE.3.15|2Pe 3:15]]; λόγος σοφίας, [[r:1CO.12.8|1Co 12:8]]; πνεῦμα σοφίας, [[r:EPH.1.17|Eph 1:17]]; σ. καὶ φρόνησις, [[r:EPH.1.8|Eph 1:8]]; σ. καὶ σύνεσις, [[r:COL.1.9|Col 1:9]];

of divine wisdom: of God, [[r:ROM.11.33|Rom 11:33]], [[r:1CO.1.21|1Co 1:21 1:24 2:7]], [[r:REV.7.12|Rev 7:12]]; πολυποίκιλος, [[r:EPH.3.10|Eph 3:10]] of Christ, [[r:MAT.13.54|Mat 13:54]], [[r:MRK.6.2|Mrk 6:2]], [[r:LUK.2.40|Luk 2:40, 52]], [[r:1CO.1.30|1Co 1:30]] [[r:COL.2.3|Col 2:3]], [[r:REV.5.12|Rev 5:12]]; of wisdom personified, [[r:MAT.11.19|Mat 11:19]], [[r:LUK.7.35|Luk 7:35 11:49]].† SYN.: σύνεσις, intelligence; φρόνησις, prudence, which with σ. make up (Arist., N. Eth., i, 13) the three intellectual ἀρεταί. σ. is wisdom primary and absolute; in distinction from which φ. is practical, σύνεσις critical, both being applications of σ. in detail (cf. Lft., and ICC on [[r:COL.1.9|Col 1:9]]; Lft., Notes, 317 f.; Tr., Syn., § LXXv; Cremer, 870 ff.). (AS)

G4605.strongs: Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine

senses: skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: [[r:ROM.16.19|Rom 16:19]], [[r:1CO.3.10|1Co 3:10]]; of the learned, [[r:ROM.1.14|Rom 1:14, 22]], [[r:1CO.1.19|1Co 1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20]]; of Jewish teachers, [[r:MAT.11.25|Mat 11:25]], [[r:LUK.10.21|Luk 10:21]]; Christian, [[r:MAT.23.34|Mat 23:34]]; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, [[r:1CO.6.5|1Co 6:5]], [[r:EPH.5.15|Eph 5:15]], [[r:JAS.3.13|Jas 3:13]]; of God, [[r:ROM.16.27|Rom 16:27]]; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, [[r:1CO.1.25|1Co 1:25.]]† SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (see: σοφία, SYN.) (AS)

G4632.strongs: a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband])
senses: a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, see MM, xxii): [[r:MRK.11.16|Mrk 11:16]], [[r:LUK.8.16|Luk 8:16]], [[r:JHN.19.29|Jhn 19:29]], [[r:ACT.10.11|Act 10:11, 16 11:5]], [[r:ROM.9.21|Rom 9:21]], [[r:REV.18.12|Rev 18:12]]; pl., [[r:2TI.2.20|2Ti 2:20]], [[r:REV.2.27|Rev 2:27]]; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, [[r:HEB.9.21|Heb 9:21]]; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, [[r:MAT.12.29|Mat 12:29]], [[r:MRK.3.27|Mrk 3:27]], [[r:LUK.17.31|Luk 17:31]]; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., [[r:ACT.27.17|Act 27:17.]] Metaphorical, of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, [[r:ACT.9.15|Act 9:15]]; ὀργῆς, [[r:ROM.9.22|Rom 9:22]]; ἐλέους, [[r:ROM.9.23|Rom 9:23]]; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. [[r:ROM.9.21|Rom 9:21]]), [[r:2TI.2.21|2Ti 2:21]]; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., [[r:1PE.3.7|1Pe 3:7]]; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., [[r:1TH.4.4|1Th 4:4]] (but see infr.); of the body, [[r:2CO.4.7|2Co 4:7]]; so perh. [[r:1TH.4.4|1Th 4:4]] (but see supr., and see: κτάομαι).† κτάομαι, -ῶμαι in pres., impf., fut. and aor., to procure for oneself, get, gain, acquire (the pf. and plpf., to have acquired, hence to possess, do not occur in NT): with accusative of thing(s), [[r:MAT.10.9|Mat 10:9]], [[r:LUK.18.12|Luk 18:12]], [[r:ACT.8.20|Act 8:20]]; with genitive pret., [[r:ACT.22.28|Act 22:28]]; ἐκ with genitive pret., [[r:ACT.1.18|Act 1:18]]; τ,ψυχὰς ὑμῶν (MM, xvi), [[r:LUK.21.19|Luk 21:19]]; τ. ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι, [[r:1TH.4.4|1Th 4:4]] (where if σ. = body, κ. must = pf., κέκτημαι; see MM, xvi; M, Th., in l; Field, Notes, 72 f. But σ. is most frequently taken as = wife; see Thayer, see word; Lft., Notes, 53 ff.; ICC, in l).† (AS)

G4650.root: apparently from the same as [[w:G4651]] (through the idea of penetrating)
G4650.strongs: to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal
senses: σκορπίζω in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, [[r:JHN.10.12|Jhn 10:12]]; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, [[r:MAT.12.30|Mat 12:30]], [[r:LUK.11.23|Luk 11:23]]; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., [[r:JHN.16.32|Jhn 16:32]]; of one who dispenses blessings, [[r:2CO.9.9|2Co 9:9]] (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).† (AS)

G4690.strongs: something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting)
senses: of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, [[r:LEV.15.16|Lev 15:16]], al.): [[r:HEB.11.11|Heb 11:11]]; metaphorically, of the divine influence, [[r:1JN.3.9|1Jn 3:9]]; by meton. (as frequently in poets), seed, offspring, posterity: [[r:MAT.22.24|Mat 22:24-25]], [[r:MRK.12.19|Mrk 12:19-22]], [[r:LUK.1.55|Luk 1:55 20:28]]" (LXX) [[r:JHN.7.42|Jhn 7:42 8:33, 37]] [[r:ACT.3.25|Act 3:25 7:5-6 13:23]], [[r:ROM.1.3|Rom 1:3 4:13, 18 9:7-8 11:1]], [[r:2CO.11.22|2Co 11:22]], [[r:GAL.3.16|Gal 3:16, 19]], [[r:2TI.2.8|2Ti 2:8]], [[r:HEB.2.16|Heb 2:16 11:18]]; pl. (FlJ, Ant., viii, 7, 6; Flat., Leg., ix, 853 with; 4Ma.18:1; in Ga, l.with, contrasted with sing., see Lft., in l; Milligan, NTD, 105 f.), [[r:GAL.3.16|Gal 3:16]]; of spiritual offspring, [[r:ROM.4.16|Rom 4:16, 18 9:8]], [[r:GAL.3.29|Gal 3:29]], [[r:REV.12.17|Rev 12:17]].† (AS)

G4615.root: perhaps from σίνομαι (to hurt, i.e. sting)

G4625.strongs: a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin)
G4625.kjv: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock
senses: (late form of the rare word σκανδάληθρον, see LS, see word) prop., the bait-stick of a trap, a snare, stumbling-block ([[r:LEV.19.14|Lev 19:14]], [[r:JDT.5.1|Jdth.5:1]]): figuratively, [[r:ROM.9.33|Rom 9:33]], [[r:1PE.2.8|1Pe 2:8]] ([[r:ISA.8.14|Isa 8:14]]; aliter in LXX; στερεὸν σκανδάλου in Aq.). Metaphorical, of that which causes error or sin;

G4633.strongs: a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively)
senses: a tent, booth, tabernacle: [[r:MAT.17.4|Mat 17:4]], [[r:MRK.9.5|Mrk 9:5]], [[r:LUK.9.33|Luk 9:33]], [[r:HEB.11.9|Heb 11:9]]; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., [[r:LUK.16.9|Luk 16:9]]; of the Mosaic tabernacle, [[r:HEB.8.5|Heb 8:5 9:2-3, 6 9:8, 21]]; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, [[r:ACT.7.44|Act 7:44]]; of its heavenly prototype, [[r:HEB.8.2|Heb 8:2 9:11]], [[r:REV.13.6|Rev 13:6 15:5 21:3]]; of the temple, [[r:HEB.13.10|Heb 13:10]]; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, [[r:ACT.7.43|Act 7:43]] (LXX); metaphorically, ἡ σ. Δαυείδ [[r:ACT.15.16|Act 15:16]] (LXX).† (AS)

G4641.root: feminine of a compound of [[w:G4642]] and [[w:G2588]]

G4623.strongs: properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water)
senses: (σιωπή, silence) to be silent or still, keep silence: [[r:MAT.20.31|Mat 20:31 26:63]], [[r:MRK.3.4|Mrk 3:4 9:34 10:48 14:61]], [[r:LUK.19.4|Luk 19:4]], [[r:ACT.18.9|Act 18:9]]; of one dumb, [[r:LUK.1.20|Luk 1:20]] (cf. 4Ma.10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, [[r:MRK.4.39|Mrk 4:39.]]† SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (which see) (AS)

G4622.strongs: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant)
senses: Σιών indecl., in NT anarth., but in LXX when used of the city of Jerusalem, ἡ Σ. (Heb. צִיּוֹן), Zion;
the mountain: in typical sense, of the Church, [[r:HEB.12.22|Heb 12:22]]; of heaven, [[r:REV.14.1|Rev 14:1.]]
The city, i.e. Jerusalem; in poetical sense;
in wider sense, of Israel: [[r:ROM.11.26|Rom 11:26]]; (with) figuratively: τίθήμι ἐν Σ λίθον, [[r:ROM.9.33|Rom 9:33]], [[r:1PE.2.6|1Pe 2:6]]" (LXX).† (AS)

G4693.root: neuter of a presumed derivative of σπέος (a grotto)
G4693.strongs: a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort

senses: (σιτίζω, to fatten) = σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: [[r:MAT.22.4|Mat 22:4.]]† (AS)

(σκότος), to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, [[r:MAT.24.29|Mat 24:29]], [[r:MRK.13.24|Mrk 13:24]], [[r:LUK.23.45|Luk 23:45]] (Rec., WH, mg.), [[r:REV.8.12|Rev 8:12.]] Metaphorical, of the mind, [[r:ROM.1.21|Rom 1:21 11:10]]" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).† (AS)

G4642.strongs: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe)
senses: (σκέλλω, to dry), hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opposite to μαλακός); metaphorically, in various uses;
of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), [[r:ACT.26.14|Act 26:14]]; λόγος, [[r:JHN.6.60|Jhn 6:60]]; ἄνεμος, [[r:JAS.3.4|Jas 3:4]]; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.† SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v (AS)

G4686.root: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of [[w:G0138]] in the sense of its cognate [[w:G1507]]
G4686.strongs: a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors)
senses: σπείρα, -ης (on this form of genitive, see M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186),
(= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil.

As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (see Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): [[r:MAT.27.27|Mat 27:27]], [[r:MRK.15.16|Mrk 15:16]], [[r:JHN.18.3|Jhn 18:3, 12]], [[r:ACT.10.1|Act 10:1 21:31 27:1]].† (AS)

G4616.strongs: byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it)
senses: as used for swathing dead bodies (cf. Hdt., ii, 86): [[r:MAT.27.59|Mat 27:59]], [[r:MRK.15.46|Mrk 15:46]], [[r:LUK.23.53|Luk 23:53]];
a garment or wrap of this material (cf. ICC, Jg, l.with): [[r:MRK.14.51|Mrk 14:51-52.]]† (AS)

G4682.strongs: apparently strengthened from through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy

G4688.strongs: a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman)

senses: a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, [[r:MRK.9.48|Mrk 9:48]] (LXX, [[r:ISA.66.24|Isa 66:24]]; cf. [[r:SIR.7.17|Sir 7:17]], [[r:JDT.16.17|Jdth.16:17]]).† (AS)
σπάω in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157), to draw: μάχαιραν, [[r:MRK.14.47|Mrk 14:47]], [[r:ACT.16.27|Act 16:27]],† (AS)

G4669.strongs: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic)
senses: intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79).
Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., [[r:MRK.15.23|Mrk 15:23.]]† (AS)

G4608.strongs: an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor

G4640.strongs: to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus)

G4698.forms: σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά
G4698.strongs: an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy
senses: the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): [[r:ACT.1.18|Act 1:18.]] Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on [[r:PHP.1.8|Php 1:8]]): [[r:2CO.6.12|2Co 6:12 7:15]], Phm 7 12 20, [[r:1JN.3.17|1Jn 3:17]]; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, [[r:COL.3.12|Col 3:12]]; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, [[r:PHP.2.1|Php 2:1]]; σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, [[r:LUK.1.78|Luk 1:78]]; σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, [[r:PHP.1.8|Php 1:8.]]† (AS)

G4683.strongs: from a derivative of the base of meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom)
senses: (σπάργανον, a swathing-band) to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: [[r:LUK.2.7|Luk 2:7, 12]] (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).† (AS)

G4692.strongs: to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly
senses: most frequently intrans., to hasten: with inf. (as frequently in cl.), [[r:ACT.20.16|Act 20:16]]; ptcp. with indic., [[r:LUK.2.16|Luk 2:16]]; with imperat., [[r:LUK.19.5|Luk 19:5-6]]; σπεῦσον κ. ἔξελθε, [[r:ACT.22.18|Act 22:18]]
to hasten, urge on, accelerate (as Hom., Od., xix, 137; Eur., Med., 152; [[r:SIR.33.8|Sir 33:8]] ([[r:SIR.36.8|Sir 36:8]]): [[r:2PE.3.12|2Pe 3:12]], R, mg. (cf. Mayor and ICC, in l, but see infr.);
to desire eagerly (find., Pyth., iii, 110; Eur., Suppl., 161; Isa 165): 2Pe, l.with, R, txt. (but see supr.).† (AS)

curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): [[r:LUK.3.5|Luk 3:5]] (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: [[r:ACT.2.40|Act 2:40]], [[r:PHP.2.15|Php 2:15]], [[r:1PE.2.18|1Pe 2:18]].† (AS)

G4606.strongs: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon

G4673.root: probably akin to the base of [[w:G4987]]
G4673.strongs: a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier

senses: (cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.) Susanna: [[r:LUK.8.3|Luk 8:3.]]† (AS)
Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret: [[r:ROM.16.25|Rom 16:25.]]† SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω (AS)

G4651.root: probably from an obsolete σκέρπω (perhaps strengthened from the base of [[w:G4649]] and meaning to pierce)

G4661.strongs: something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty
senses: (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: [[r:LUK.11.22|Luk 11:22.]]† (AS)

G4648.strongs: to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard
G4648.kjv: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark
senses: ακοπέω, -ῶ (σκοπός), to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), [[r:2CO.4.13|2Co 4:13]], [[r:PHP.2.4|Php 2:4]]; with accusative of person(s), [[r:ROM.16.17|Rom 16:17]], [[r:PHP.3.17|Php 3:17]]; before μή, [[r:LUK.11.35|Luk 11:35]]; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), [[r:GAL.6.1|Gal 6:1]] (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).† SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω (AS)

G4620.strongs: a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food)
senses: (σιτομετρέω, [[r:GEN.47.12|Gen 47:12, 14]] *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω), a measured portion of food: [[r:LUK.12.42|Luk 12:42]] (for exx. in π., see Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 103.1).† (AS)

G4611.forms: Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, genitive, ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ)
G4611.strongs: Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem

G4676.strongs: a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse)
senses: handkerchief, kerchief: [[r:LUK.19.20|Luk 19:20]], [[r:ACT.19.12|Act 19:12]]; used as a head covering for the dead, [[r:JHN.11.44|Jhn 11:44 20:7]] (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).† (AS)
σινιάω (σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω, to sift, winnow: figuratively, [[r:LUK.22.31|Luk 22:31.]]† (AS)

G4637.strongs: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion)
senses: (σκηνή), to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), [[r:REV.7.15|Rev 7:15]]; before ἐν, with dative of person(s), [[r:JHN.1.14|Jhn 1:14]]; id. with dative loc., [[r:REV.12.12|Rev 12:12 13:6]]; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), [[r:REV.21.3|Rev 21:3]] (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).† (AS)

G4634.strongs: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes)
senses: (σκηνή, πήγνυηι), prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, [[r:LEV.23.34|Lev 23:34]], al.; see Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: [[r:JHN.7.2|Jhn 7:2.]]† (AS)

G4628.strongs: through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank)

G4614.strongs: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia
senses: Σινά (-ᾶ, Rec.), indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό (Heb. סִינַי), Sinai ([[r:EXO.19.11|Exo 19:11]], al.): [[r:ACT.7.30|Act 7:30, 38]], [[r:GAL.4.24|Gal 4:24-25]]† (AS)

G4638.strongs: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul)
senses: (σκηνόω), a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling ([[r:PSA.132.5|Psa 132:5]], al.), [[r:ACT.7.46|Act 7:46]]. Metaphorical, of the body: [[r:2PE.1.13|2Pe 1:13-14.]]† (AS)
σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον (σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), eaten of worms: [[r:ACT.12.23|Act 12:23]] (cf. [[r:2MA.9.9|2Ma 9:9]], and see MM, xxiii) † (AS)

G4609.forms: Σίλας, -α (accusative to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.5)

G4691.strongs: a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk)
senses: in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: [[r:ACT.17.18|Act 17:18.]]† (AS)
(σκηνή, ποιέω), making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: [[r:ACT.18.3|Act 18:3.]]† (AS)

(σκληρός), to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), [[r:ROM.9.18|Rom 9:18]]; T. καρδίας ([[r:PSA.95.8|Psa 95:8]]), [[r:HEB.3.8|Heb 3:8, 15 4:7]]. Pass., to become hardened: [[r:ACT.19.9|Act 19:9]], [[r:HEB.3.13|Heb 3:13]].† (AS)

G4612.strongs: a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron)

G4607.strongs: a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans)
senses: (Lat.; sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii), a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): [[r:ACT.21.38|Act 21:38.]]† (AS)

G4602.root: apparently from σίζω (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush)

G4627.strongs: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing)
senses: (σκάπτω), anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: [[r:ACT.27.16|Act 27:16, 30 27:32]].† (AS)
(= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία ([[r:1MA.8.3|1Ma 8:3]]) or Σ. as here), Spain: [[r:ROM.15.24|Rom 15:24, 28]].† (AS)
(in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form frequently in π.), -οῦ, ὁ, Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: [[r:2CO.1.19|2Co 1:19]], [[r:1TH.1.1|1Th 1:1]], [[r:2TH.1.1|2Th 1:1]], [[r:1PE.5.12|1Pe 5:12]].† (AS)

G4636.strongs: a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit)
senses: = σκηνή, a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: [[r:2CO.5.1|2Co 5:1 5:4]].† (AS)

G4647.root: perhaps from the base of [[w:G4628]] and [[w:G3700]]
G4647.strongs: withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability)
senses: In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, [[r:2CO.12.7|2Co 12:7]] (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).† (AS)

G4656.strongs: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively)
senses: (σκότος), to darken: [[r:REV.9.2|Rev 9:2 16:10]]. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., [[r:EPH.4.18|Eph 4:18]] (cf. σκοτίζω).† (AS)

G4696.strongs: a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace
senses: In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically,
of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): [[r:2PE.2.13|2Pe 2:13.]]† (AS)

G4689.strongs: to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend")
senses: σπένδω to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): [[r:PHP.2.17|Php 2:17]] (see Lft., in l), [[r:2TI.4.6|2Ti 4:6]] (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

G4657.root: neuter of a presumed derivative of [[w:G1519]] and [[w:G2965]] and [[w:G0906]]
G4657.strongs: what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure)
senses: refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): [[r:PHP.3.8|Php 3:8.]]† (AS)

G4649.strongs: perhaps akin to through the idea of concealment; compare); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal
senses: a mark on which to fix the eye ([[r:WIS.5.12|Wis 5:12, 21]], al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: [[r:PHP.3.14|Php 3:14.]]† (AS)

G4658.strongs: a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage
senses: Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: [[r:COL.3.11|Col 3:11.]]† (AS)
(σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, [[r:SIR.27.13|Sir 27:13]] *), to live riotously: [[r:1TI.5.6|1Ti 5:6]], [[r:JAS.5.5|Jas 5:5]] (Polyb.).† SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv) (AS)

G4629.root: from a derivative of σκέπας (a covering
G4629.strongs: perhaps akin to the base of through the idea of noticeableness); clothing
senses: (σκεπάζω, to cover), a covering, esp. clothing: [[r:1TI.6.8|1Ti 6:8.]]† (AS)

G4679.strongs: to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error
senses: (σοφός), to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), [[r:2TI.3.15|2Ti 3:15]] (cf. [[r:PSA.19.8|Psa 19:8]] ([[r:PSA.119.98|Psa 119:98]]). As depon., -ομαι;
intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 ([[r:1KI.5.11|3Ki 5:11]]), [[r:ECC.2.15|Ecc 2:15]], and frequently in [[r:SIR.7.5|Sir 7:5]], al.);
trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., [[r:2PE.1.16|2Pe 1:16]] (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).† (AS)

G4695.strongs: to stain or soil (literally or figuratively)
senses: σπιλόω to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, [[r:JAS.3.6|Jas 3:6]], Ju 23.† (AS)

G4694.strongs: a ledge or reef of rock in the sea
senses: (on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41),
poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.).
In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).† (AS)

G4667.strongs: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor
senses: Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: [[r:REV.1.11|Rev 1:11 2:8]].† Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, [[r:REV.1.11|Rev 1:11 2:8]] T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).† (AS)
As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: [[r:REV.4.3|Rev 4:3]] (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).† (AS)

G4665.strongs: the emerald or green gem so called
senses: (and in late writers also ὁ), emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): [[r:REV.21.19|Rev 21:19.]]† (AS)
